Read CLAUDE.md, the supplied north-star.json and /Users/m/.codex/plugins/cache/kan-tools/day/0.12.0-beta.3/skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md. Git-first recording due day#168/kan#197. Do not invent witnesses or reconstruct excluded claims, and don't claim current live-log access from the frozen supplied record. Frozen commit and exact tracked path/SHA256 manifest are in ../recovery-replay-identity.json.

Scope: new pure src/evidence_recovery_replay.rs, tests/evidence_recovery_replay.rs, independent .design/tools/recovery_replay_vectors.py and fixture, and scripts/recovery_replay_negative_controls.py. Governing documents: .design/kan-v2-recovery-bundle-codec.md, especially Next draft checkpoint: pure observation replay, and parent .design/kan-v2-recovery-bundles.md. Treat ancestor raw review reports as evidence of their stated frozen scopes, not permission to infer parent completion.

Replay takes owner-pinned immutable member/candidate/observation slices and an optional separately retained checkpoint. It verifies the entire observer chain, exact initial M1/frontier and greedily partitioned loss coverage, every candidate's content address/authorized member key/authenticated expected length, one restoration per physical candidate, historical R1 and fully re-audited virtual output before O1, attempt/intent/failure/observed relations and external checkpoint matching. Incomplete-copy membership losses retain their derived UnverifiedMembership basis and no authenticated expected length; restoration doesn't promote their provenance. No external checkpoint means no rollback protection; an earlier checkpoint can't detect deletion of a later unpinned suffix. Observed publication is an attributed historical claim, not proof of a current durable file or writer activation.

Challenge semantic false-but-signed histories, complete-vs-partial recipe, metadata/writer contradictions, candidate selection before vs after intents, missing/corrupt/orphan union, loss omissions/duplicates/partitioning, skipped suffix validation, cross-context checkpoints, resource bounds/cancellation and caching. The scan-byte metric is documented input passes, not RSS or exact CPU cycles; decode/signature operations are individually bounded. No file opener/schema writer, signing producer, crash/job/RPC/UI or durability authority is introduced. All full bundle/frontend acceptance remains open.

Python independently constructs signed histories over valid source members built by the independent member fixture constructor, computes state/R1/O1 itself and verifies selected-output writer signatures. It explicitly is not a general second source-member semantic validator. Independently investigate beyond its corpus; do not call a Rust-derived expected value an independent oracle. Include probe traces and compiled selected semantic guard removals. Distinguish incorrect acceptance/projection from diagnostic-only failures, redundant guards or compile failures.

Verify exact export path set/hashes AND Git blobs at pinned commit before/after, using explicit repo /Users/m/code/kan-tools/kan/.worktrees/kan-v2-recovery-replay. Only initial extra north-star.json. Put all raw logs, probes, mutations, failures and REPORT.txt under review-evidence/. Restore tracked bytes and remove any temporary probe copies. No parent edits/Git writes/network/live archives/keys/traffic/install/.lake/own target or unrelated process kills. Do not run revert_v2.py from the export. One heavy job at a time, shared target/four jobs; cargo clean -p kan first.

Bounded baseline: v2-crypto evidence_recovery_replay, inherited evidence_recovery_member_corrections and evidence_recovery_member_review_regressions; all-target strict v2 Clippy/fmt; independent Python replay --check. Read retained author qualification rather than assuming its claims. Reproduce focused replay controls plus independent probes/selected new controls as needed for concrete concerns; avoid rerunning unchanged historical 27+17 mutation suites or unrelated compatibility/performance/Node matrices.

Write a full evidence/requirement/finding report and one hard APPROVE / APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS / REDIRECT / BLOCK verdict. Explicitly identify prerequisites before this can become a physical writer consumer; do not round pure replay acceptance up to full recovery or frontend completion.

Separate scope B: the inherited 5edb505 consumer follow-through after the b11cbf4 correction review. Read the unmodified .design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-member-corrections-opus/evidence/REPORT.txt (C-F1..C-F6) and author .design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-member-consumer-followups-author/REPORT.md. C-F2 adds a partial-copy occurrence-loss Python vector and promoted CP11; C-F3 promotes CP01/exact MAX_REQUEST; C-F4 refuses empty service-request CIDs even without bytes, in Rust and Python; C-F5 corrects comments and removes the vacuous assertion. This last member runtime change is one guard. Reproduce the three focused controls (empty-request-cid, retain-issuer-length, request-bound-edge) and the whole-runtime reversion to cd0a9ff with the named empty_service_request_cid_refuses_without_an_original regression, using an explicit repo git show/restore. # kan — agent working notes

You are building `kan`: a local-first, provenance-preserving memory substrate for
AI agents, in Rust. This file orients you; the authoritative design is in `docs/`.

## Read first, in order
1. `docs/HANDOFF.md` — **historical**: the original bootstrap brief, kept as
   a record of the starting point. Useful for the vocabulary map; its scope
   and open-choices sections are long resolved. Read it for background, not
   for current state.
2. `docs/SPEC.md` — AUTHORITATIVE data model, identity model, anchors, computable
   relations, the fold algorithm, storage, and the v1 scope fence. If anything
   here conflicts with SPEC.md, SPEC.md wins.
3. `docs/ROADMAP.md` — the current shipped baseline, active RFC 3 issue graph,
   repository boundaries, and document precedence.
4. `docs/SETUP-TODO.md` — the historical bootstrap checklist, with its active
   network phases redirected to the current roadmap.

## The one non-negotiable invariant
The fold reads morphisms; it never mutates objects. **No operation destroys a
subject.** Identity and status are computed objects (path-spaces / posets),
collapsed to flat values only at the display boundary, never in the store.
If a change would let one actor's write mutate or destroy another's data, it's wrong.

## What to build first (the spine — do NOT build the cathedral)
Local-only, one human, one-or-more local agents, one repo, no sync:
Claim + DAG-CBOR CID + signing → local append-only log (source of truth) →
disposable SQLite index → the fold (identity-before-state, same enrichment,
decategorify only at render) → git anchors + computable relation providers →
CLI + MCP server with budgeted context assembly.

Explicitly OUT for the local spine: sync/atproto/lexicons, TUI, web dashboard,
editor extensions, >2 trust enrichments, enforcement hooks, incremental fold.
The local-only spine shipped through v0.3.0-beta.1. Do not treat that historical
scope fence as an open-ended ban or use ADR-35's old version table as the
current plan. Read `docs/ROADMAP.md` first for sync-adjacent work; public
ATProto publication is governed by RFC 3 (currently Review) and issues
#235–#241 under epic #29. The older sync staging design remains context for the
separate HostedRelay track.

## House rules
- Rust. Use `atproto-repo` + `atproto-dasl` for MST/CAR/CID (`atrium-crypto`
  for signing), so local-only and future atproto are the same on-disk
  artifact. **Not** `atrium-repo` — ADR-1 originally picked it, but ADR-11
  found a confirmed data-loss bug in its MST (filed upstream:
  atrium-rs/atrium#343) and ADR-12 records the switch. Before trusting any
  storage-layer crate here again, run **both** checks before building on it,
  not after:
  1. **Reachability** (ADR-11/12) — sequential inserts, check full
     reachability after every single one, not just at the end.
  2. **Conformance** (ADR-90) — compare the artifact against an *independent
     implementation*, not against our own reading of the spec. Reachability
     alone is not enough: `atproto-repo` 0.14.5's MST never split, losing
     nothing while writing a repo no conformant implementation agrees with
     (kan#204) — a quadratic write cliff and a wrong root CID that the
     reachability rule passes cleanly. `tests/mst_conformance.rs` is the
     working example; `src/mst/` is what it cost — kan now owns the MST
     outright, because a `[patch.crates-io]` fix reaches CI but never reaches
     `cargo install kan`.
- Correctness before performance. The reference fold recomputes; caching and
  incremental folds are follow-ups, optimized only against passing fixtures.
- A persistence change is also a surface-contract change. Update
  `tests/fixtures/read-write-surface.tsv`, the typed capability at the mutation
  site, and `tests/surface_conformance.rs` together; derived media never become
  authority merely because they are persisted or fast.
- The fold is a pure, deterministic function of (claim set, enrichment). Guard this.
- Affordance, not enforcement — agents act; the record is made legible; drift
  surfaces in the graph as data. Do NOT port crosslink's blocking hooks.
- One surface: CLI + MCP for v1. The owner explicitly authorized a v2 operator
  front end on 2026-10-18: `.design/kan-v2-operations.md`. It reads the same
  operations API as the CLI; this exception does not add a workflow authority.
- Provenance is sacred: never fabricate or drop `cites` edges.

## Smell test
The local-only path must be *dramatically* simpler than the multi-actor path
(one log, all subjects Local, no SameAs stitching, no contest stage, latest-wins).
If it isn't, the abstraction is wrong — stop and reconsider.

## CLI vocabulary (git-like, verb-first)
Declared in four AX-driven phases ([`ADR-0032`](adrs/32-verb-lexicon-reorganized-by-ax-phase-mcp-tool-surface-catches-up-to-the.md)) — `kan --help`
reflects this order directly, so treat it as the source of truth over this
line if they ever drift:
- Recording: `observe | plan | decide | block | resolve | result`
- Structuring: `same | relate | mark`
- Correcting: `retract | reject`
- Recalling: `show | status | issues | context [--budget N]`
- Sharing: `publish <subject>` — writes the subject's signed claims into the
  tracked `.claims/` directory (ADR-43). Writes files; never runs git.
- Outside the four phases (setup/tooling, not a claim-graph verb): `mcp [install]`

## Scope boundary: kan vs. `day`, the companion tool
kan owns a feature iff it needs a new/existing `ClaimBody`/`ClaimKind`/
`Anchor`/`RelationKind` variant, or is a pure read/fold over the claim graph
that needs no memory of *when* or *why* to call it. If a feature is buildable
entirely as a calling convention over existing primitives (subject naming,
`cites`, `artifacts`) with no data-model change, it's process/workflow and
belongs in the companion tool that consumes kan via CLI/MCP — not a new mode
of kan itself. Full rationale and worked examples (why `kan session
start/end` was removed, why a proposed vector index still belongs in kan):
[`ADR-0018`](adrs/18-the-kan-companion-tool-scope-boundary-kan-session-removed.md).

That companion tool now exists: **`day`** (`kan-tools/day`, on crates.io) —
the structured *process* layer to kan's structured *knowledge* layer. It
holds teloi, process atoms, and drift assessment entirely as conventions
over kan's existing verbs (`telos/<slug>` and `atom/<slug>` subjects), needs
no kan data-model change, keeps no store of its own, and shells out to the
`kan` binary rather than linking it. ADR-42 records what its existence
settles — including the two things it put back on kan: an "in tension with"
edge (`RelationKind::InTensionWith`, since shipped — ADR-46), and day
writing through kan's CLI, making kan's write-verb ergonomics a dependency
of a program rather than only of agents. Send a process/workflow feature
request there, not here.

meant and what exists, and to say so plainly.

### Step 0 — Establish that you are that reviewer

Read this before Step 1. If you wrote any of the code under review, **every
clause of the paragraph above is false about you**: you did write it, you have
just reported it complete, and you carry the reasoning this review exists to
audit from the outside.

That is the default case when this command is invoked as a slash command in the
session that produced the work, so treat it as the expected situation, not an
edge case.

1. **Where the harness can dispatch a fresh agent, offer to.** Hand it the design
   doc, the kan subject, and the diff range, and let it report back. In Claude
   Code that is the Agent tool with a **general-purpose** agent.
2. **It must be cold, not a fork.** `subagent_type: "fork"` inherits the parent's
   full conversation, so it arrives already holding the rationalisations this
   step exists to strip. It would reproduce the problem while appearing to solve
   it. A context-inheriting reviewer is not an independent one.
3. **Offer, do not force.** An in-context pass is fast and catches the obvious,
   and the operator may legitimately want one. Ask; abide by the answer.
4. **If you proceed in-context — because the operator declined, or because no
   such capability exists — say so in your output, in the verdict itself**, in
   roughly this form:

   > **Declared conflict of interest.** The premise of this review is a reviewer
   > with no stake. I wrote this code. I have compensated by reproducing every
   > claim against the running binary rather than by reading my own tests, but an
   > independent reviewer would still be better placed to find what follows.

   A review that is not independent and does not say so is worse than an openly
   self-audited one, because the verdict reads identically either way.

This is not ceremony. Two of the three defects behind day#101 were found by a
review of code the same session had written, and both were found by *executing*
it against hostile input rather than by re-reading it — which is the step an
author is least likely to take, because they already believe they know what it
does. When you cannot get independence, buy back what it was protecting: run the
thing, do not re-read your own summary of it.

### Arguments

- `--design <slug>`: the design doc to audit against (`.design/<slug>.md`)
- `--subject <subject>`: the kan subject carrying this work's claims
- `--pr <number>`: audit a GitHub PR's diff instead of the working branch

If none are given, infer the target from the branch and the most recently modified
design doc, and **state the inference explicitly** before proceeding — a review of
the wrong thing is worse than no review.

### Step 1 — Recite the north star, from the record

Do not paraphrase from memory and do not invent a north star.

1. If any `telos/*` subjects exist in kan, read them (`kan show telos/<slug>`).
   Those are the north star. Quote them.

   **What you gathered is subjects on record, not teloi in play.** It does not
   filter retracted ones; day's own reader does
   (`src/hooks.rs:render_teloi`), and the two lists differ in this repo
   today. A retracted telos quoted as the north star is a review measuring
   against a target the project abandoned — so confirm each one is live, and
   treat the list as a starting set, not an answer.
2. If none exist, fall back to this repo's orientation docs (`CLAUDE.md`, an
   authoritative spec, the design doc's own Summary). Quote the specific lines.

   Before you take that branch: **"none" here has three causes** — a project with
   no teloi, a log you could not read, and a filter that no longer matches what
   kan emits. Only the first licenses the fallback. The third is what happened
   here once already, and it reported `none` in a repo with nine live teloi,
   silently, for as long as nobody checked; the second is the reason the Context
   section tells you to report a failed kan read rather than continue past it.
   Confirm the log is readable and genuinely empty of `telos/` subjects before
   concluding there is no north star.
3. State which telos or stated purpose **this particular work** was meant to
   serve. If you cannot find one, that is itself a finding: record it and say
   so — unstated purpose is where drift enters.

Where several teloi are in play, name the tension between them. Work that
silently optimizes one at another's expense is the single most common real
finding this review produces.

### Step 2 — REQ/AC coverage table

For each REQ and AC in the design doc, produce a row: the requirement, the
verdict (`met` / `partial` / `unmet` / `unverifiable`), and **the evidence**.

Evidence means a file path and line range you actually read, or command output
you actually ran. It does not mean:

- the design doc asserting its own requirement is satisfied,
- a commit message, changelog entry, or ADR saying the work was done,
- an agent's summary of what it did.

Quote the code. If a requirement's satisfaction cannot be established from the
artifacts, mark it `unverifiable` and say what would be needed — never round it
up to `met`.

### Step 3 — Verify the evidence yourself

Run the project's own verification, in this order, and report raw results:

1. Build (`cargo build --workspace --all-targets`, `npm run build`, `make`, …)
2. Tests (`cargo test --workspace`, `npm test`, …)
3. Lint (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, …)
4. Format (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, …)

If a claimed test exists, **run that specific test and confirm it fails when the
behavior is broken** where you can do so cheaply. A test that passes
unconditionally is not coverage. If you cannot run something, say so — do not
report unrun commands as passing.

### Step 4 — Scope-narrowing check

Grep the diff, the design doc, and any new decision records for scope-narrowing
language: `out of scope`, `deferred`, `follow-up`, `future work`, `for now`,
`TODO`, `later`, `v2`.

Judge each instance independently:

- **Legitimate**: named before implementation, recorded, and genuinely separable.
- **Suspicious**: narrowed *during* implementation, or narrowing exactly the part
  that was hard, or deferring the requirement that made the feature worth doing.

Quote each instance and give a verdict per instance. A design that ended up
smaller than it started is not automatically wrong, but it needs to have been
decided, not drifted into.

### Step 5 — Forbidden-pattern re-introduction

Check the diff against this repo's own stated house rules — the ones in its
`CLAUDE.md` and its decision records, not generic best practice. For kan and day
specifically, that includes:

- The fold reads; it never mutates. No operation destroys a subject.
- Affordance, not enforcement — no blocking hooks, no gates on agent action.
- One surface (CLI + MCP); no second UI sneaking in.
- Provenance is sacred: `cites` edges are never fabricated or dropped.
- day stores nothing of its own; durable state is kan claims.

For any other repo, derive the equivalent list from its own docs and say which
rules you derived and from where.

### Step 6 — Verdict

End with **exactly one** of these four, in bold, with a one-paragraph rationale:

- **APPROVE** — requirements met, evidence verified independently, no drift.
- **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS** — sound and shippable; specific, named gaps that
  do not undermine the north star. List them as concrete follow-ups.
- **REDIRECT** — the work is competent but pointed somewhere other than the
  stated telos. Say precisely where it diverged and what it should serve instead.
- **BLOCK** — a correctness, safety, or invariant violation. Name the invariant
  and the exact code that violates it.

Do not soften the verdict to be agreeable. Do not inflate it to seem rigorous.
"APPROVE" on genuinely good work is a useful signal that only stays useful if
you are willing to say it.

### Step 7 — Record it

```bash
day review record <subject> \
  --verdict APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOW-UPS \
  --rationale "<one line>" \
  --cites <cid of the design/plan claim being audited>
```

The verdict must be one of the four values above and must cite the claim it
audits; `day` rejects anything else rather than recording a verdict nobody can
trace back to what it judged.

Record each material finding as its own claim citing that verdict, so a later
session can find the finding without re-reading this whole review:

```bash
kan observe "<finding>" --subject <subject> --cites "$VERDICT"
```

If the verdict is BLOCK or REDIRECT, also mark the subject:

```bash
kan mark <subject> --value Blocked   # check `kan mark --help` for valid values
```

### Step 8 — What comes next

```bash
day next adversarial-review
```

Report what the graph says rather than naming a step from memory. A project
that loops review back into design has declared that; another may terminate
here.

**A round of fixes to a BLOCK gets its own review** — kan's ADR-52, stated here
rather than left as something a person has to remember. It has now been
validated **eight times** in this repo, and three times consecutively in one
milestone, where each round found defects the previous round's author could not
see. The severity moved as it went: round 1 found code defects, round 2 found a
bug the round-1 fix introduced, and round 3 found that *"the code changes in this
round are correct… what is wrong is the evidence."*

So when this review returns BLOCK, the fixes are a new implementation, not an
addendum to the reviewed one, and they are reviewed as such. The author of a fix
round is the least able person to see what it missed, which is the same argument
that makes this atom cold in the first place (Step 0).

If the fix round closes a finding, its commit carries a `Demonstrated-by:`
trailer from `scripts/revert-demo.py` — revert the fix, watch the named test
fail, restore, watch it pass. A round that says "fixed and the suite is green"
has asserted the weaker of the two things, and day#116's first instance is a fix
whose entire reversion left 337/337 tests passing.

## Rules

- **Probes leave traces.** Verifying a defect by running the real command
  against the real log appends real claims — that is how a junk
  `telos/review-probe` subject ended up in day's own record and then in its
  session-start context. Probe in a scratch repo, or retract in the same
  breath. An assessment that pollutes the record it assesses is measuring its
  own footprint.
- **Check the other side of every interface.** The most serious finding this
  review has produced was a hook wired to an event whose stdout never reaches
  the model — invisible to every test, because the tests asserted what the
  tool printed rather than whether anything read it. Read the docs for the
  thing being integrated with; do not infer its behavior from your own side.
- Do NOT modify code. This atom reads and judges; fixing is a separate atom.
- Do NOT trust the design doc, the ADRs, or the commit messages about whether
  the work was done. They are claims about the work, not the work.
- Do NOT report a command as run if you did not run it.
- Every finding cites a file path and line, or command output.
- If the design doc itself is wrong or incoherent, say that — auditing against a
  bad specification faithfully is still a failed review.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify export path set + SHA256 vs manifest, and git blob ids at pinned commit."""
import hashlib, json, os, subprocess, sys
REPO = "/Users/m/code/kan-tools/kan/.worktrees/kan-v2-recovery-replay"
EXPORT = os.path.join(REPO, ".local-state/reviews/recovery-replay")
MAN = os.path.join(REPO, ".local-state/reviews/recovery-replay-identity.json")
allowed_extra = set(sys.argv[1:])  # top-level extras allowed (north-star.json, review-evidence)
m = json.load(open(MAN))
commit = m["commit"]; files = m["files"]
present = set()
for root, dirs, fs in os.walk(EXPORT):
    rel_root = os.path.relpath(root, EXPORT)
    if rel_root == ".":
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in allowed_extra]
    for f in fs:
        rel = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(rel_root, f))
        if rel in allowed_extra: continue
        present.add(rel)
missing = sorted(set(files) - present); extra = sorted(present - set(files))
bad = []
for p, h in files.items():
    fp = os.path.join(EXPORT, p)
    if os.path.islink(fp) or not os.path.isfile(fp): continue
    if hashlib.sha256(open(fp, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != h: bad.append(p)
head = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
commit_full = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "rev-parse", commit + "^{commit}"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
ls = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--full-tree", commit], capture_output=True).stdout
tree = {}
for ent in ls.split(b"\0"):
    if not ent: continue
    meta, path = ent.split(b"\t", 1)
    mode, typ, oid = meta.decode().split()
    tree[path.decode()] = (mode, typ, oid)
tree_missing = sorted(set(tree) - set(files)); man_not_tree = sorted(set(files) - set(tree))
blob_bad = []
for p in files:
    if p not in tree: continue
    fp = os.path.join(EXPORT, p)
    data = open(fp, "rb").read()
    oid = hashlib.sha1(b"blob %d\0" % len(data) + data).hexdigest()
    if oid != tree[p][2]: blob_bad.append(p)
# git object hashes of tracked blobs vs manifest sha256 (from repo object db)
print(json.dumps({"commit": commit, "commit_resolved": commit_full, "repo_HEAD": head,
  "manifest_files": len(files), "export_files": len(present), "missing": missing, "extra": extra,
  "sha256_mismatch": bad, "tree_files": len(tree), "tree_not_in_manifest": tree_missing,
  "manifest_not_in_tree": man_not_tree, "blob_mismatch": blob_bad}, indent=1))
ok = not (missing or extra or bad or tree_missing or man_not_tree or blob_bad) and commit_full == commit and head == commit
print("IDENTITY_OK" if ok else "IDENTITY_FAIL")
EOF

1	# Proposal: KNB1 recovery bundle codec and member commitment
2	
3	This freezes the proposed byte/schema choices for independent design review of
4	`kan-v2-recovery-bundles.md`. It is not an implemented format. No writer may use
5	these bytes as a compatibility promise until the design and independent vectors
6	are reviewed. The parent bundle requirements and publication distinctions apply.
7	
8	## Identities and canonical values
9	
10	The physical database encoding is UTF-8. Creation must set `PRAGMA encoding =
11	'UTF-8'` before creating tables; opening must verify the existing encoding is
12	UTF-8 and refuse UTF-16 rather than attempting conversion. This is a proposed
13	format requirement; no creation/opener exists yet.
14	
15	The outer SQLite `application_id` is `0x4b4e4231` (KNB1), `user_version=1`.
16	The logical member is explicitly profile 2 or 3; its ordinary archive/scope/issuer
17	binding is preserved. An owner supplies an independently retained random 32-byte
18	bundle ID and observer DID key. Neither is learned as authority from the file.
19	A bundle backup preserves that ID; a new observation branch needs explicit owner
20	selection or a new bundle identity, not a silent history merge.
21	
22	Canonical DAG-CBOR and low-S P-256 signature encoding follow the already reviewed
23	service-attestation codec, with a separate signature domain and a separate closed
24	schema. Integers are nonnegative and at most `9007199254740991`. Identifiers use
25	canonical CID encoding (raw/SHA256 for object bytes; DAG-CBOR/SHA256 for statements)
26	and validated static `did:key` P-256 authors. Unknown fields, alternate encodings,
27	unknown versions/events, malformed/non-low-S signatures and trailing bytes refuse.
28	A rejected record is not skipped while continuing the observation frontier.
29	
30	The envelope is the canonical DAG-CBOR map `{statement: bytes, signature: bytes}`.
31	The statement bytes encode exactly:
32	
33	- `version`: 1.
34	- `domain`: `tools.kan.recovery.observation.v1`.
35	- `bundle`: 32 bytes, the external physical-copy pin.
36	- `profile`: 2 or 3, the logical archive profile.
37	- `archive`, `scope`: 32 bytes each; `issuer`, `observer`: canonical DID strings.
38	- `sequence`: positive integer; `previous`: statement CID or null at genesis.
39	- `sampledAt`: Unix milliseconds, informational rather than ordering authority.
40	- `event`: one closed event name below; `body`: its closed event map.
41	
42	Compute the statement CID from its exact canonical bytes. Sign the canonical
43	DAG-CBOR preimage map `{domain: "tools.kan.recovery.observation.v1", statement:
44	<statement CID link>}` using the existing P-256 identity signer. This follows the
45	service proof's domain-separated CID preimage pattern, with a different domain.
46	The statement's domain field must equal that same literal. The statement CID
47	hashes statement bytes, not the envelope/signature. Envelope maximum
48	16 KiB includes both encoded byte strings. Every body repeats the complete pinned
49	context through the common statement; no observation inherits an unverified
50	identity from an earlier row.
51	
52	## Initial member commitment M1
53	
54	`SHA256` consumes the following byte stream. `F(x)` means an unsigned 64-bit
55	big-endian byte length followed by x. `N(n)` is unsigned 64-bit big-endian n.
56	The pure framing layer bounds issuer text to 1..80 UTF-8 bytes; it does not
57	validate a DID. A full member requires a canonical static P-256 DID (56..80
58	ASCII bytes), a stricter semantic check. DIDs use UTF-8; CID frames use canonical binary CID bytes; record/envelope frames
59	use exact original canonical bytes. Empty sections still include their count.
60	
61	1. ASCII `tools.kan.recovery.member.v1` followed by one zero byte.
62	2. `N(profile)`, `F(archive)`, `F(scope)`, `F(issuer)`.
63	3. `F("plan")`, `N(0)` for profile 2. Profile 3 instead has `N(1)`,
64	   `F(exact original plan envelope)`.
65	4. `F("original-membership")`, `N(count)`, then canonical object-CID text lexical
66	   order: `F(binary CID)`, `N(expected length)`. Profile 2 has zero entries.
67	5. `F("records")`, `N(count)`, then increasing contiguous sequence:
68	   `N(sequence)`, `F(manifest bytes)`, `F(receipt bytes)`, `F(issuer proof bytes)`.
69	6. `F("original-objects")`, `N(count)`, then canonical object-CID text lexical
70	   order: `F(binary CID key)`, `N(actual retained byte length)`, `F(raw bytes)`.
71	
72	The original object key is retained even when its raw bytes do not hash to it.
73	Missing objects are absent, not fabricated empty rows. A present zero-length
74	corrupt object is a present row with length zero and an empty frame. Staged/orphan
75	objects are included. A valid identifier with corrupted bytes is representable;
76	a malformed key, duplicate logical key, unreadable SQL cell, unknown schema or
77	non-BLOB object cell (including TEXT with identical encoded bytes), or
78	raw object larger than 4 MiB refuses initial creation and retains the source and
79	failed output. This is a bounded capture format, not arbitrary SQLite forensics.
80	A later format for oversized forensic fragments needs a separate explicit recipe;
81	it must not silently truncate a row to fit M1.
82	
83	M1 intentionally excludes rebuildable indexes/lookup columns, bundle identity,
84	observations and restoration candidates. Those are bound by their own signed
85	context/history. Identical member evidence in two physical bundles has the same
86	M1. The source metadata frontier includes both manifest and issuer-statement CIDs,
87	not just a high-water sequence. For empty history both are null.
88	
89	## Event bodies
90	
91	All digests below are 32 bytes; `member` uses M1, `output` uses O1, and
92	`restorations` uses R1. O1 has exactly M1 framing with the initial domain replaced
93	by ASCII `tools.kan.recovery.output.v1` followed by a zero byte. It commits to the
94	fully verified selected output rather than the original damaged member. All attempt IDs are owner-generated
95	16-byte values. A `frontier` is a closed map `{through, manifest, attestation}`
96	with both links null iff `through=0`. Nonempty links have DAG-CBOR/SHA256 codec.
97	
98	- `created`: `{recipe: 1, member: digest, frontier}`. Exactly sequence 1; no later
99	  created event. The logical metadata/proof chain must independently verify.
100	- `unavailable`: `{member: digest, entries: [...]}`. One to 32 entries, each
101	  `{occurrence, cid, expectedLength, state}`. `occurrence` is a positive member
102	  sequence or null for a staged/orphan object; `expectedLength` is an expected
103	  length from authenticated metadata or a completely verified copy recipe. It is null
104	  for an unreferenced object without an authenticated length, including membership-only
105	  coordinates in an incomplete copy. Their basis is derived from the fixed member
106	  (issuer metadata, verified copy recipe, unverified retained membership, or original
107	  object key); readers must expose that basis alongside each loss. The signed wire
108	  does not add a second, independently editable basis field. `state` is `missing` or
109	  `corrupt`. No metadata-corruption state pretends a broken proof is trustworthy.
110	- `restored`: `{member: digest, cid, length, candidate}`. `candidate` is the raw/SHA256 CID of the
111	  verified candidate and equals `cid`; length is 1..4 MiB. The target must exist
112	  in member metadata, original membership or original object keys. Every member-derived authenticated expected length must agree; conflicting
113	  references refuse. Do not read an incomplete-copy membership length as an
114	  expected length. Restoration inherits and exposes the coordinate basis,
115	  including UnverifiedMembership; content-address verification does not authenticate
116	  source membership, even when valid original bytes were already present. Unknown orphan
117	  length is established by this verified candidate, not invented historical data.
118	- `publication-intent`: `{attempt, member: digest, restorations: digest,
119	  output: digest, frontier}`. `output` is the expected O1 of the deterministic
120	  selected standalone output, checked before signing intent. Exactly one intent
121	  per attempt ID. No path/command is trusted as signed executable routing data.
122	- `publication-observed`: `{attempt, intent, output: digest, frontier}`. `intent`
123	  cites the exact prior intent statement. `output` is O1 of the fully verified
124	  standalone output, must equal the cited intent output commitment, using selected valid objects and unchanged original metadata.
125	  It reports an observed durable output; it never records service activation.
126	- `publication-failed`: `{attempt, intent, reason}`. Closed reason enum:
127	  `source-changed`, `invalid-candidate`, `destination-conflict`, `budget`, `io`,
128	  `verification`. It makes no assertion that an output file does not exist.
129	
130	The 32-entry limit is subordinate to the 16 KiB envelope bound. Use another
131	linked observation when encoding would exceed that bound. All created/member
132	references must equal the independently recomputed original M1. Unavailable
133	entries must match the sampled original rows and the member-derived coordinates, lengths and basis; restoration never deletes them. Restore and publication events
134	must reference the member fixed at creation, not a silently revised member.
135	
136	R1 is `SHA256(domain || N(count) || items)`, where domain is ASCII
137	`tools.kan.recovery.restorations.v1` plus zero byte, and items in canonical CID
138	text lexical order are `F(binary CID) || N(length) || F(candidate bytes)`.
139	R1 includes every candidate with a matching restored observation strictly before
140	that intent's sequence. There is no optional unsigned selection list. Each must
141	verify against its content address and all member-derived authenticated expected lengths. A verifier
142	replays the chain to reconstruct this exact historical set; candidates appended
143	after the intent never enter its R1. A different candidate set requires a new
144	attempt and intent. This makes restart verification independent of a lost job
145	process or an externally remembered subset.
146	
147	The virtual standalone output contains exactly the union of original object
148	keys, authenticated record object references and original membership keys.
149	Every key needs verified bytes of all member-derived authenticated expected lengths: use its verified
150	restoration candidate from this R1 set when present, otherwise its valid original
151	bytes. A still-missing/corrupt key refuses publication, including staged/orphan
152	keys. Never drop a corrupt orphan to make verification pass, add an unreferenced
153	new object, or use a candidate recorded after the intent. Recompute expected
154	output O1 from this deterministic union and unchanged records/plan/membership; both intent and
155	publication-observed must equal it and the original metadata frontier. The normal
156	standalone verifier still independently validates all signatures and profile
157	completion. A partial profile-3 member has no KNB1 publication operation; it stays
158	a retained recovery artifact until a separate metadata-extension design exists.
159	
160	## Exact initial loss coverage
161	
162	Derive one expected coordinate for each `(occurrence sequence, object CID)` in
163	member metadata. The coordinate algorithm preserves occurrences; it does not
164	collapse history by CID. The current service-request profile additionally refuses
165	an empty-request CID or a request CID referenced by two distinct occurrences: exact request bytes fix one
166	writer, operation and position, and an empty byte string cannot be a signed
167	service request, so such metadata cannot be satisfied. A future
168	payload profile permitting shared bytes needs its own reviewed binding rules. Add a null-occurrence coordinate for each
169	original membership key or original object key that has no occurrence reference;
170	never add a second null entry for a CID already represented by occurrences.
171	All authenticated lengths for a CID must agree or creation refuses. The expected
172	length is that agreed authenticated value. For membership-only keys in an
173	incomplete profile-3 copy, no source digest authenticates the membership yet:
174	retain the exact rows in M1, mark the coordinate basis UnverifiedMembership, and
175	report expectedLength null. A raw original key without authenticated length also
176	has expectedLength null. These are observed rows, not proof of source membership;
177	missing or substituted rows cannot be detected until the complete recipe verifies.
178	
179	Sample each coordinate against the original member objects. Missing rows produce
180	missing entries; a wrong hash (or an empty unreferenced original) produces a
181	corrupt entry. Hash-valid bytes with a disagreeing authenticated length refuse as
182	invalid member metadata; they must not be mislabeled corrupt or repairable. An
183	unverified membership length neither classifies original bytes nor constrains a
184	restoration candidate. Available entries produce no unavailable event. Non-BLOB cells refuse creation under the M1 rule.
185	Sort occurrence entries first by ascending numeric sequence then canonical CID
186	text; sort null entries last by canonical CID text. No duplicate coordinate is
187	allowed. The concatenation of creation's unavailable events must equal this exact
188	ordered loss vector: omissions, extra entries, duplicate entries, conflicting
189	states or altered expected lengths refuse verification.
190	
191	These events occur immediately after created, before restoration/publication.
192	Partition greedily into the largest consecutive prefix of at most 32 entries
193	whose canonical signed envelope fits 16 KiB; signatures have fixed 64-byte width.
194	No empty event is permitted. Empty loss coverage means created alone. Verifiers
195	recompute the same vector and partition; an unavailable event after that initial
196	coverage is invalid. Damage to the physical bundle after creation is an integrity
197	failure against its fixed M1, not permission to rewrite member bytes or insert a
198	new claim that retrospectively changes the initial sample. Preserve such media
199	and recover the bundle from verified backups; arbitrary forensic repair remains
200	outside KNB1.
201	
202	## Physical tables
203	
204	All tables use the exact frozen column order; any extra table/index/trigger/view
205	refuses normal bundle open. DDL must be generated once by the implementation and
206	pinned by canonical schema fixtures before a writer is accepted.
207	
208	- `bundle_identity(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), bundle BLOB,
209	  observer TEXT, profile INTEGER, archive BLOB, scope BLOB, issuer TEXT)`.
210	  Byte-width/profile/DID validation is mandatory on read and before writes.
211	- `member_records(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, manifest BLOB, receipt BLOB,
212	  envelope BLOB)`: sequence positive, manifest/receipt each 1..65536 bytes,
213	  envelope 1..16384 bytes; all NOT NULL. No ordinary `commits` or `attestations`
214	  table exists in this outer format.
215	- `member_objects(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
216	  original bytes 0..4194304, key canonical but payload may be corrupt.
217	- `member_plan(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), envelope BLOB
218	  NOT NULL)`: no rows for profile 2, exactly one 1..4096-byte row for profile 3.
219	- `member_membership(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, length INTEGER NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
220	  profile 3 only, canonical CID and length 1..4194304.
221	- `observations(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, envelope BLOB NOT NULL)`:
222	  canonical contiguous observation chain, envelope 1..16384 bytes.
223	- `restored_objects(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
224	  bytes 1..4194304 and exact content address. Every row must have one matching
225	  restoration observation; every restoration observation must have its candidate.
226	
227	SQL constraints enforce local type/size bounds; the verifier independently
228	checks all semantic/profile/cardinality/chain conditions. In particular, empty
229	observation history cannot convert a bundle into a standalone archive.
230	Publication constructs an entirely separate normal profile; changing a marker
231	or renaming a table never constitutes publication.
232	
233	## Required pre-implementation review
234	
235	Review the event state machine, all cross-file crash outcomes and the ability to
236	resume or record failure without rewriting history. Freeze actual DDL, canonical
237	positive/re-signed-negative vectors and an independent Python encoder/verifier
238	before storage mutations are implemented. Pin M1 and R1 against independently
239	constructed empty, staged, missing, corrupt, restored and partial-copy fixtures.
240	Whole-output verification must include ordinary writable schema, original writer
241	signatures, issuer proof chain and profile-3 completion; M1 alone proves none of
242	those properties. The observer can report evidence, but cannot grant admission,
243	erase historical loss or assert a fabricated complete source-copy recipe.
244	
245	### Publication state and replay rules
246	
247	An attempt ID has exactly one intent. It may have zero or more failed observations
248	and at most one observed publication. A failure is evidence of an unsuccessful
249	check, not a terminal assertion that no valid output exists. Explicit resume may
250	therefore append observed after failure when it verifies that same attempt's
251	selected commitment and owner-specified output. No failed or second observed
252	record may follow observed for that attempt. A changed selection or different
253	output identity requires a new attempt ID and intent. Independent verifiers must
254	validate these relationships from the complete observation chain, not a mutable
255	status column.
256	
257	Creation's single publication transaction includes a created event plus enough
258	unavailable events to cover every unavailable expected occurrence, every
259	missing/corrupt original-membership key (including unreferenced staged objects),
260	and every corrupt retained orphan row. Missing orphans with no surviving expected
261	coordinate cannot be invented. Exact repeated restoration is idempotent: return
262	the prior candidate/observation, without a new row or signature. A candidate
263	insert without its observation, or observation without its candidate, refuses.
264	
265	The owner-selected observation frontier is an external checkpoint, comprising
266	sequence and statement CID under the full bundle/observer binding. Verifiers
267	must prove that checkpoint belongs to the observed chain and distinguish it from
268	any later verified extension. A file cannot supply its own rollback-detection
269	checkpoint. No cross-copy anti-equivocation beyond the explicitly pinned chain
270	is claimed.
271	
272	### Checkpoints and multiple completed outputs
273	
274	Several attempt IDs may each reach publication-observed. Each creates a separate
275	physical standalone output with the member's logical archive identity; none
276	activates a service. The owner must select exactly one live writer and fence the
277	others through the separately authorized activation workflow. The bundle cannot
278	promise that privileged manual configuration obeyed that workflow.
279	
280	Every successful mutation/job result returns the verified observation frontier
281	(sequence plus statement CID and full binding), including a committed failure
282	observation. The owner verifies and durably retains it outside the bundle before
283	advancing the recovery UI's independently checkpointed status. On restart the
284	owner supplies the latest retained checkpoint; valid extensions are reported
285	separately until retained. A tail truncated after the latest external checkpoint
286	is not detectable. The online observer key can attribute new statements but does
287	not itself provide an independent tamper-evidence or non-equivocation witness.
288	An uncertain response may require explicit inspection and checkpoint advancement;
289	do not derive the external pin from the bundle being verified.
290	
291	### Scope-C follow-through before format acceptance
292	
293	The governing bundle design's "custody and owner-visible limits" section is part
294	of this codec contract: pre-open path checks cover all participating databases;
295	partial-copy restart provenance is external job state only; forensic-only source
296	cells are a named recovery gap; unrecoverable staged/orphan keys explicitly block
297	publication. None changes the byte recipes or adds a silently unsigned field to
298	the closed observation schema. Draft SQL and wire fixtures still require their
299	own independent review before acceptance or any storage writer.
300	
301	## First implementation checkpoint: observation authentication
302	
303	`src/evidence_recovery_observation.rs` implements only bounded canonical wire
304	validation, static P-256 owner pins, observer signature attribution and contiguous
305	observation predecessor links. `Authenticated` has private construction and
306	carries no bundle-completeness, member-truth or publication-state authority.
307	`sign_claim` is a pure signer and round-trip validator; its caller must establish
308	the permitted operation and semantic truth before using it. There is no storage
309	consumer, mutation, file routing, checkpoint acceptance or browser API here.
310	
311	Independent Python fixtures exercise the six event forms, exact statement/CID/
312	signature bytes, maximum wire shapes and re-signed hostile cases. Their member,
313	restoration and output digest values deliberately do not establish a valid full
314	bundle. A wire-valid claim may still be false; complete bundle verification must
315	reject those false claims. The Rust API does not provide JSON serialization or
316	accept a caller-constructed predecessor as authenticated history.
317	
318	The accompanying SQL fixture is a **draft** local-constraint schema, exercised
319	in memory with no publication markers. The M1/O1/R1 Python oracle is a **draft**
320	framing oracle, not a signed-record or complete-member verifier; synthetic record
321	bytes in its framing cases do not qualify any archive. Neither draft is accepted
322	as a storage compatibility promise by this checkpoint. Before a bundle writer:
323	implement and independently qualify streaming commitment computation, complete
324	member/proof validation, exact loss partitioning, candidate/history consistency,
325	publication replay and external-checkpoint validation; then freeze their complete
326	cross-implementation vectors and DDL. All recovery writer/job/RPC/UI criteria stay
327	open until their real operations and crash outcomes are tested and reviewed.
328	
329	### Second independent review decisions
330	
331	Observer authority is a separate role and signature domain from archive issuer
332	authority. The wire codec permits explicitly pinned equal observer/issuer DIDs;
333	it never treats an observer signature as an archive proof. Distinct-key policy
334	belongs to owner configuration. Recovery job configuration should default to a
335	separate observer key and disclose explicit reuse; equality in the wire is not
336	proof of independent authorities or compromise isolation. This interpretation
337	of parent REQ-1 is recorded rather than silently requiring a new wire restriction.
338	The same-key role fixture pins this decision.
339	
340	Refusal reason strings in the cross-implementation fixtures identify their
341	single-fault cases. They do not define a total precedence for inputs with several
342	independent faults: Rust and Python may name different first faults while both
343	refuse. No authorization or state transition may depend on which diagnostic
344	string wins. Acceptance and byte identity remain the interoperability contract.
345	
346	The expanded fixtures now distinguish canonical CID text order from binary order
347	for unavailable entries, original membership, original objects and R1 candidates.
348	The draft DDL bounds identifier text by bytes, excludes embedded NUL and requires
349	printable ASCII; complete canonical DID/CID validation remains a verifier duty.
350	SQLite's lossless affinity coercion is not a promise about caller bind types:
351	writers must bind typed values and readers must still check stored types.
352	
353	An authenticated expected object length above 4 MiB also refuses KNB1 creation
354	as `forensic-recovery-required`, even when no oversized physical row survives.
355	Do not truncate the expected length or drop that reference to fit the format.
356	Retain source and failed output; the generic manifest schema's larger integer
357	range does not widen this proposed recovery format's representable object size.
358	
359	## Next checkpoint draft: bounded streaming framing
360	
361	The draft `evidence_recovery_commitment` module computes M1/O1/R1 incrementally.
362	Its caller supplies section counts and strictly increasing canonical CID-text
363	order; it does not allocate an archive-sized sort or payload buffer. Separate
364	membership/record/object stages enforce counts and contiguous record positions.
365	Any rejected builder operation poisons the builder, so ignoring an error cannot
366	produce a digest over fewer records. Empty corrupt originals remain representable;
367	restoration candidates must be nonempty and match their raw CID.
368	
369	Owner-selected item, work-byte, time and cancellation limits bound computation;
370	hashing polls at most every 64 KiB. Work-byte accounting includes framing and,
371	for restoration, both candidate verification and commitment hashing. It does not
372	bound prior caller acquisition or arbitrary filesystem stalls. The caller remains
373	responsible for authorized bounded source reads and complete member semantics.
374	DID/record/plan truth, candidate membership and full state replay are not supplied
375	by these framing digests. This draft has no storage consumer. Author qualification passes eight commitment
376	tests against independent Python vectors and nine compiled controls, with strict
377	v2 Clippy and formatting. Evidence is in
378	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-author/`. Fresh independent review
379	remains pending; full member and state verification are separate prerequisites.
380	
381	
382	### Streaming review follow-through
383	
384	Actual Opus 5.5 review of a8927a6 found no production defect and returned
385	APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS; full raw evidence is retained in
386	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-opus/`. RA3/RA4 section/count/size
387	probes are promoted. Test-only cancellation injection qualifies polling within
388	hashing without timing sleeps; the original independent timing probe and its
389	recorded limits remain preserved. These follow-through tests pass author qualification: ten integration functions,
390	two deterministic polling units and thirteen compiled controls, plus strict
391	Clippy/format and the independent oracle. Evidence is in
392	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-followups-author/`. Fresh scope-B
393	review with the member checkpoint returned APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS; its raw
394	record is in `.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-member-opus/`. The Rust multibyte
395	issuer edge and stale test-provenance text are corrected below.
396	
397	The 1..80-byte framing issuer bound is explicit above and now shared by the
398	Python oracle. UTF-8 is pinned for future physical creation and opening. An O1
399	digest from the framing builder alone still authenticates no output bytes:
400	full object/writer/profile verification must precede publication. None of these
401	changes accepts the physical format or closes parent acceptance criteria.
402	
403	## Next verifier checkpoint: logical member and initial availability
404	
405	The pure member verifier takes an owner-pinned context and borrowed, ordered
406	record, membership and original-object slices. Its caller must acquire those
407	bytes with bounded reads before calling; this is not a SQLite opener. The physical
408	reader must reject noncanonical original CID text before constructing typed CIDs;
409	parsing a spelling and silently normalizing it is not source validation. Explicit
410	item/input-byte/time/cancellation limits bound this invocation. It stores only
411	bounded metadata coordinates, never copies the whole payload collection. Hashing
412	polls per 64 KiB; canonical decoding, request verification and signatures are
413	individually bounded operations with cancellation checks around them.
414	
415	Independently verify the contiguous issuer chain, admitted versus retained-copy
416	purpose, static service writer form, per-writer position/predecessor, unique
417	operation, the service operation-to-slot commitment and consistent slot bindings. Profile 3 additionally binds its plan,
418	original membership and retained-prefix metadata digest. An unfinished prefix is
419	reported as incomplete; matching metadata alone does not certify missing writer
420	signatures or retained bytes. No standalone publication capability is returned.
421	
422	Every retained length must be positive, at most 4 MiB, and agree across references
423	and original membership; referenced service requests additionally cannot exceed
424	the service MAX_REQUEST bound. Contradictory shared service-request CIDs refuse
425	even with no payloads present. Retain raw corrupt/empty originals in M1. Verify each
426	present object's hash once and sample every occurrence separately; unreferenced
427	membership/original keys receive null-occurrence loss coordinates. A hash-valid
428	request that fails its writer signature or exact manifest binding is invalid
429	member evidence, not a repairable missing-byte condition. Missing/corrupt requests
430	remain unavailable, with writer verification still outstanding. Loss output is
431	strict occurrence/CID-text order, followed by null coordinates in CID-text order.
432	
433	This checkpoint must be qualified before it can feed full observation replay.
434	Greedy signed-loss partitioning, historical restoration/output selection, replay,
435	checkpoints, physical schema and all storage mutations remain separate work.
436	
437	
438	At 3169a0a the logical-member draft passed author qualification: 16 Rust functions,
439	independent signed Python fixtures, eight semantic controls (one additional
440	cancellation control survives because framing refuses later), strict Clippy and
441	formatting. Raw results are in
442	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-member-author/`. Its completed independent review
443	and correction requirements follow; this is not full bundle acceptance.
444	
445	### Member review corrections: evidence basis and contradictory metadata
446	
447	Fresh actual Opus 5.5 review of 5e54513 returned APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS; raw
448	evidence is retained in `.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-member-opus/`. Before
449	replay consumes this component, A-F1 governs in favor of refusing hash-valid
450	bytes with false authenticated lengths. A-F2 is resolved by a typed per-loss
451	basis: incomplete-copy membership-only coordinates remain visible as unverified
452	observations with no authenticated expected length. M1 retains the exact claimed
453	rows/lengths. No external copy-job authority is invented. Complete recipes and
454	issuer references retain their stronger, independently checked basis.
455	
456	A-F3 adopts early refusal of reused service-request CIDs. A-F4 deterministic
457	reviewer probes are promoted; timing evidence remains a separate recorded limit.
458	The wire's expectedLength is derived under these rules; basis is recomputed from
459	the same fixed member, not trusted from an extra signed field. Any consuming
460	API/UI must preserve the distinction, including when no external rollback
461	checkpoint exists. These corrections still confer no publication authority.

463	### Correction-review consumer follow-through
464	
465	The fresh review of b11cbf4 is retained in
466	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-member-corrections-opus/` (APPROVE WITH
467	FOLLOW-UPS). C-F1 defines restored/R1/output lengths as member-derived
468	authenticated expectations, never unverified retained claims. A restoration must
469	expose its recomputed basis even for an already-available key with no initial
470	loss. C-F2 adds partial-copy occurrence-loss vectors and the independent CP11
471	regression; C-F3 pins the exact MAX_REQUEST boundary. C-F4 refuses empty service
472	request CIDs with or without an original row, in Rust and the projection oracle.
473	C-F5 restores accurate probe comments and removes the vacuous immutable-input
474	assertion. Fresh review of this follow-through accompanies the replay checkpoint.

476	## Next draft checkpoint: pure observation replay
477	
478	Replay is over immutable caller-acquired member, candidate and observation slices,
479	under independent bundle/issuer/observer pins and an optional externally retained
480	checkpoint. It first audits the member and fixes M1/frontier. It authenticates
481	one contiguous observer chain from genesis, compares creation to that member,
482	and requires the exact greedily partitioned initial loss vector before any
483	restoration or publication. A late, omitted, repeated or altered loss refuses.
484	The member-verifier review must be resolved before qualifying this consumer.
485	
486	Each physical candidate must have exactly one restored observation, target an
487	existing member key/reference, match its content address and every authenticated
488	expected length. Incomplete-copy membership-only lengths are retained claims,
489	not candidate constraints. Replay returns the member-derived basis for every restoration, including
490	an already-available key with no initial loss;
491	restoration cannot promote UnverifiedMembership into authenticated source evidence.
492	No unsigned candidate, duplicate restoration, hidden subset or new orphan is
493	accepted. An intent commits to all candidates observed before it. Replay computes
494	that historical R1 and deterministic output union, re-audits the virtual output
495	(including writer signatures and complete profile-3 recipe) and only then computes
496	O1. The virtual audit is not a physical standalone-schema or durability check.
497	Originals and later candidates never silently replace historical selections.
498

500	observed result, no later failure or second observed for that same attempt.

517	the selected candidate set is unchanged. All collections are bounded by charged
